What is measured, and what is not

Per-camera lookup — measured

"Did this plate pass this camera?", asked of each camera in turn. Over held-out vehicles: 92.0% of the hits reported are real, and 89.6% of the cameras a vehicle actually passed are found. Base rate 6.2%.

Multi-camera routes — not established

When a second camera is reported it is, by construction, one with no independent label. A separate verification round found nine of ten proposed cross-camera links to be different vehicles, so those sightings are shown as CANDIDATES for an officer to confirm, never as an asserted route.

Why the reading can be wrong and the answer right

The index stores the recogniser's probabilities, not its final text. GJ03DH7859 is stored as GJ03OH7859 — a D read as an O — and the query still finds it, because D was a close second at that timestep. String matching misses it entirely.

Honest limits. The index holds 1,406 sightings from five ten-minute windows. A city-scale index of millions would be a harder discrimination and this precision would fall — by how much has not been measured, so it is not claimed.
Precision and recall measured on vehicles the recogniser never trained on, with the operating threshold chosen before the numbers were read off. Camera positions are the real GPS in the platform database.
